Manx: Ea 5. Yn Fer-ynsee Cadlagh
Vershion aashagh
Va fer-ynsee cliaghtey goaill snap beg dy chadley dagh fastyr ayns y çhamyr-vrastyl.
Tra ren ny schoillaryn briaght jeh cre’n oyr v’eh jannoo shoh, ren eh gra dy row eh
goll dys Çheer ny Hashlishyn dy loayrt rish shenn gheiney creeney.
Fastyr dy row, er laa erskyn towse çheh, ren paart jeh ny schoillaryn hene tuittym nyn
gadley ayns y çhamyr-vrastyl. Tra va’n fer-ynsee troiddey roo, ren ad gra:
“Agh vainshter, ren shin goll dy veeiteil rish ny shenn gheiney creeney ayns Çheer ny
Hashlishyn.”
“Dy firrinagh?” ren yn fer-ynsee briaght jeu lesh pooar. “As cre ren ad gra?”
“Ren shin briaght row fer-ynsee schoill çheet dys shen dagh fastyr, agh ren ad gra
nagh row ad rieau er nakin lhied y phersoon."
No 5. The Sleepy Teacher
Easy version
A teacher used to have a nap every afternoon in the classroom. When the students
asked him why he did this he said that he went to the Land of Visions to talk to old
wise masters.
One afternoon, on an exceedingly hot day, some of the students themselves fell asleep
in the classroom. When the teacher was telling them off, they said:
“But sir, we went to meet the old wise masters in the Land of Visions.”
“Indeed?” the teacher demanded. “And what did they say?”
“We asked if a school teacher came there every afternoon, but they said they’d never
seen such a person.”
